findings.where: Screen 9 (A wire between poles), text and picture
findings.what: "The same rule gives the force" never says which way the rule runs for a wire: fingers along the current, curled toward the field. No curl is drawn either. So puzzle 12 (Current along i), which asks for that direction, can only be solved through its hint. Add two short sentences: point your fingers along the current, curl them toward the field, and your thumb gives the force. Optionally add a third: Fleming's left hand agrees.

findings.where: Screen 7 (Swap the order), text and axes readout
findings.what: Only i × j = k and j × i = −k are taught. Puzzle 12's Why? rests on k × i = j, and no screen states it. The brief promised "i × j = k, and so on round". Add one sentence: round the cycle, j × k = i and k × i = j.

The screen says "Only its part square to the handle, |F| sin θ, turns the bolt" but never gives the reason. The part along the handle points straight through the bolt, so it has nothing to turn about. The screen also never says θ is the angle between r and F, or that the size is |r||F| sin θ. In a steps lesson the explain text is not shown, so this central why is missing. The screen has room: it is 48 words now.

The swing goes 90° → 30°, holds 0.5 s, then makes one eased 1.3 s move from 30° to −30° (th = 90 − 60·go(1.8,1.0) − 60·go(3.3,1.3)). It passes 0° at full speed and never stops there. So the state the text and the brief name as the one thing to see never rests on screen: along the handle the parallelogram is flat, the arrow is gone and the readout says "0 N m, no arrow". The film goes from about 7 N m out of the nut straight to values into the nut. Hold about 0.6 s at 0° before swinging past.

There are six footnote markers: [^1] twice, then [^2] to [^5]. [^3] ("The dot product is a plain number, but the cross product is an arrow") and [^5] ("It acts square to both the current and the field") mark plain statements, not a rule or value he would look up on a job. The bold summary line repeats [^1]. Keep [^1], [^2] and [^4], and drop the rest.

"IlB sin θ = 10 × 0.2 × 0.8 = 1.6 N" drops the sin 90° = 1 step, though the readout shows "× sin 90°". It also never says that l is the length of wire in the field or that θ is the wire's angle to the field. The sentence is 22 words. Write "10 × 0.2 × 0.8 × sin 90° = 1.6 N" and split the sentence.

findings.where: Symbols on screens 9, 10 and 12 (text and the "I = 10 A" / "I = 4 A" labels)
findings.what: The vector-letter styling does not include I, so the current prints upright and plain while B prints bold italic. Inside "IlB" no letter is styled at all. In this sans font, capital I and lowercase l look the same, so "IlB" reads as "IIB", and the label "I = 4 A" could be read as l. Style I as a quantity, and style l on its own inside IlB.

It asks for exactly the case screen 3 has just stated: 150 N, 0.3 m, 30°, "the moment halves to 22.5 N m". So he can answer from memory without working it out. Change the values, for example 150 N at 30° and 0.2 m out, which gives 15 N m. The slips would then be 25.98 N m with cos and 30 N m with no angle.

findings.where: Puzzle 6 (Undo or do up), task and hint
findings.what: The task says "clockwise", and screen 5 has just said "Clockwise, it points in to do it up". So the puzzle is matched by words, not by using the hand. The "Out of the nut" hint then says "Your thumb points down", which gives the answer away. Let the picture show the turn and ask him to read it. Have the hint send him back to curling from r toward F.

In "Anticlockwise, as you look down on the nut, it points out of the nut to undo it", "anticlockwise" belongs to the turn but "it" means the arrow. The sentence also carries three ideas. Write it as: "Turn anticlockwise, seen from above, and the arrow points out of the nut. That undoes it." Do the same for the clockwise sentence.

The last sentence is 24 words with three ideas in it. The screen also never links the area to the moment Dan already works out, the push times its distance. It says the arrow is "along the bolt" but not why: it is square to both r and F. Split the sentence and add those two short points. The screen stays under 90 words.

"The shaded area is the moment's size, and the right-hand rule gives its direction" stays under the wire screens. Those screens shade nothing, and the quantity there is a force, not a moment. Make the caption general, or say what both pictures share.

The brief's lesson-6 row promised a link back to lesson 3: three forces whose lines do not meet at a point leave a moment, so they cannot balance. The link appears nowhere, not in the steps, the explain or the practice. One sentence on screen 7 or in the explain would deliver it.

It is 441 words long and retells all twelve screens with their numbers. It includes an instruction ("You can drag sideways on the picture to turn the view") and talks about the lesson's own structure ("Some screens show an idea. The rest ask you to try it."). Cut it to what the picture shows and how to read it: r, F, the shaded area, the moment arrow, the curl and the poles.

findings.where: Puzzle 12 (Current along i), axes triad at 360 px
findings.what: The i, j, k triad is small: 30 px arrows at bottom left. The j arrow is the shortest because it points into the screen, so the j and k labels sit almost on top of each other. The answer is along −j, so the j axis is the one he most needs to read. Enlarge the triad or turn the view so j is not foreshortened.
